trait.description: Percentage of the plot covered, 1 = poor to 7 = good establishment
Judgment of homogeneity of the accession, 1 = homogeneous to 7 = mixed

categories: 1: Most plants are the same (up to 10% different)
3: Over half of plants are the same (10%–30% different)
5: Less than half of plants are the same (30%–50% different)
7: Over 50% of the plants are different, completely mixed plot; will need to be excluded from analysis

trait.description: Score for the overall amount of side branches of representative plants in a plot, ignoring very small and spindly branches, ranging from 1 = no branches to 7 = bushy plant with many major lateral branches

categories: 1: Low number or no secondary branches
3: Some branches (30 – 50% of the primary branch length has secondary branching)
5: Branched (50 – 70% of the primary branch length has secondary branching)
7: Highly branched (above 70% of the primary branch length has secondary branching)

trait.description: Four categories of growth habit described in images on the scoring card. Here the focus lies on whether branching is present from the base of the plant and if a main inflorescence can be identified

categories: 1: Not branched at base, usually with a clearly defined terminal panicle
3: Some branching from the base; no significant panicles on branches in the basal area (thus, this is not worth harvesting)
5: Branching from the base with more significant panicles
7: Main panicle is difficult to identify

trait.description: Stems are broken or detached, assessing the percentage of the plot affected
Stem of the plant is not emerging straight up from the soil but has a kink at the base, growing along the ground before rising; assessing the percentage of the plot affected
Plants are prostrate, on or near the ground, with intact stems; assessing the percentage of the plot affected
The angle at which the majority of plants are leaning, measured between the vertical axis and the horizontal axis

categories: 1 < 22.5° inclination or deviation of the stem from the vertical (i.e. most plants are upright)
7< 90° (i.e. most plants are on or very close to the ground)

trait.description: The angle at which the majority of panicle axes are leaning, measured between an upright panicle on the verticle and a panicle pointing towards the ground

categories: 1< 45° inclination or deviation of the panicle from the vertical (i.e. most panicles are upright)
7< 180° (i.e. most panicles are pointing towards the ground)

trait.description: Height of the most representative plants of the plot, usually from the middle of the plot, measured with a long measuring stick from soil to the tip of the panicle. If more than one distinct phenotype is present, more than one plant may be recorded in a new row of the spreadsheet, with all phenotypes that are differing recorded separately
Length of the primary panicle measured with the same stick. Measured from the base of the panicle to the tip
Thickness of the stem measured with calipers at the middle of the bottom third of the plant stem

method.methodName: Stem diameter near plant base measurement

trait.description: Thickness of the stem measured just underneath the main panicle

method.methodName: Stem diameter under the panicle measurement

trait.description: Count of the number of significant panicles, i.e., larger panicles, near the top of the plant, harvestable, that provide a major contribution to the seed harvested from the plant
Grain persistence in the plant at physiological maturity. Assessing how easy seeds fall off the panicle upon light touch: 1 = No seeds falling to 7 = a lot of seeds falling

categories: 7: Majority of seeds is falling, “raining” seeds, and a large number of seeds present on the ground at measurement

trait.description: Classified into one of the three categories: glomerulate, intermediate, or amarantiform

categories: 1: Glomerulate – glomerules with globose shape, resembling “bulbous clusters”
3: Intermediate – panicles have both amarantiform and glomerulate traits, resembling fingers with glomerules
5: Amarantiform – glomerules with elongated shape, resembling “fingers”

trait.description: Scored from 1 = lax (loose) with panicle axes easily visible to 7 = tight and compact panicles

categories: 1: Lax (loose) – glomerules sparsely spaced, panicle axes easily visible
3: Intermediate – glomerules tighter but with panicle axes still visible
7: Compact – glomerules tightly packed, no panicle axes visible

trait.description: Scored from 1 = no leaves to 7 = many leaves

categories: 1: leaves are present in less than ⅓ of the panicles
3: leaves are present in more than ⅓ but less than ¾ of the primary, sporadic, and not dense panicles
5: leaves present in ¾ to of the entire primary axis, frequent but not dense leafiness
7: many leaves present throughout the primary axis

trait.description: Categorized according to the color scoring card
Categorized into green (13), red (4), or no pigmentation (15)
Presence (1) absence (0) scoring of stem streaks or stripes
Presence (1) absence (0) scoring of pigmented axils
Leaves of the stem are categorized into two groups: rhomboidal (1) and triangular (2)
Leaf margins are classified into 3 groups
Phenological growth stage; very important to record at mature phenotyping

trait.traitName: Number of plants harvested per plot
trait.description: Total number of plants that were harvested of the plot.

method.methodName: Number of plants harvested per plot counting

trait.description: Count the number of plants that were harvested seperately from the majority of the plot, as representative plants.

method.methodName: Number of representative plants harvested counting

trait.description: Cutting plants at the very base with secateurs and drying the entire above-ground section of the plant. Recording total dry weight and number of plants that make up total dry weight. Divide total weight with number of plants to give weight per plant
If possible, root biomass could also be measured (especially when plants are growing in sandy soil)
Harvesting the panicles remaining per plot while excluding borders, and adding the weight to that from the four representative plants, seed dried in oven to constant weight
Seed mass of approximately four representative plants that were harvested from the center of the plot (seed should be dried to constant weight)

method.methodName: Seed yield for representative plants measurement

trait.description: Total harvested seed mass per plant may be calculated from number of plants harvested and the seed mass of all plants in the plot (SdWtpPlot/PltNoHv)
Thousand Grain Weight (TGW), the weight of 1000 seeds
Yield/ above-ground biomass
Hectoliter weight, or specific weight of seeds: Estimation of density, determined by weighing all seeds fitting into a 100 ml volume
Average area of the seeds from image analysis
Average perimeter of the seeds from image analysis
Numerical seed color red value, RGB R Component from image analysis
Numerical seed color green value, RGB G Component from image analysis
Numerical seed color blue component, RGB B Component from image analysis
Tested in petri dishes (%)
